label: Bid & Tender Management
title: Bid Management Software for Construction | CA-Vault
desc: Collect compliant bids, manage tender documents and get a line-by-line bid comparison the moment the tender closes. Built for unit-price construction contracts.
short: Collect compliant bids and get the comparison without rebuilding spreadsheets by hand.
h1: Construction Bid Management Without the Spreadsheet Shuffle
lead: Collect bids, manage tender documents, enforce submission requirements and generate bid comparisons without manually rebuilding your analysis.
shotCaption: Every bid, line by line, against the average bid price. Lowest and highest prices are highlighted for you.
answerTitle: What is construction bid management software?
answer: Construction bid management software runs a tender in one place: it distributes the tender documents, collects each bidder’s prices against the same schedule of prices, and compares the bids once the tender closes. In CA-Vault the comparison is produced from the submitted bids themselves, so nobody re-keys numbers from PDFs into Excel.
problem: On a unit-price tender, every bidder prices the same list of items. When those bids arrive as PDFs by email, someone has to type every unit price into a spreadsheet, check the arithmetic and chase incomplete submissions. It is slow, and it is exactly where errors creep in.
capsTitle: See every bid side by side

caps.t: One schedule of prices for every bidder
caps.d: Bidders price the same items, quantities and units, so bids are comparable from the first line to the last.
Bidders complete the required information before they can submit, which cuts down on non-compliant bids.
Review unit prices and totals line by line, with section subtotals, against the average bid or your budgeted price.
Share the bid review with the owner or keep it on file without rebuilding it in another tool.

steps.d: Set up the schedule of prices and attach drawings, specifications and other tender documents.
Bidders receive the documents and price the schedule online. Contractors are invited free of charge.
When the tender closes, the bid comparison is generated from the submitted prices.
The awarded prices become the contract’s schedule of prices, ready for administration.

faq.q: Can CA-Vault compare bids automatically?
faq.a: Yes. Because every bidder prices the same schedule of prices inside CA-Vault, the line-by-line comparison is generated from the submissions when the tender closes. You can review it on screen or export it to PDF or Excel.

faq.q: Do bidders have to pay to submit a bid?
faq.a: No. Contractor invitations are unlimited and free for contractors on the Tender plan and above.

faq.q: Is CA-Vault only for unit-price tenders?
faq.a: Unit-price contracts are where CA-Vault is strongest, because the whole platform is organised around the schedule of prices. Ask us in a demo how your other contract types would be set up.

faq.q: What happens to the bid prices after award?
faq.a: The awarded bid becomes the starting point for contract administration, so quantities, unit prices and totals do not need to be entered again for progress billing and payment certification.

label: Contract Administration
title: Construction Contract Administration Software | CA-Vault
desc: Keep the contract, its schedule of prices, documents, RFIs, changes and payments in one connected project record shared by owner, consultant and contractor.
short: Keep contract information, records and workflows organised throughout the project.
h1: Construction Contract Administration in One Connected Record
lead: Administer the contract from award to closeout with the schedule of prices, documents, RFIs, changes and payments all tied to the same record.
shotCaption: Every contract with its total value, remaining value, invoiceable amount and progress at a glance.
answerTitle: What is construction contract administration software?
answer: Construction contract administration software manages what happens after a contract is awarded: the records, questions, changes, inspections, progress and payments that flow between the owner, the consultant and the contractor. CA-Vault keeps those workflows attached to one contract so each party works from the same information.
problem: Most contract administration is spread across inboxes, spreadsheets and shared folders. Each party keeps its own version, and reconciling them takes time nobody budgeted for.
capsTitle: Three parties. One contract. One record.

caps.t: A contract lifecycle you can see
caps.d: Each contract moves through clear stages: Draft, Tendering, Post-tender, In Progress and Completed.
Schedule of prices, provisional items, documents, RFIs, submittals, change orders, progress reports and invoices sit in one place.
Items waiting on your review land in your ActionBox, with reminders, so approvals do not stall in an inbox.
Bring the contractor, owner and sub-consultants into the same contract rather than forwarding files between systems.

stepsTitle: How a contract moves through CA-Vault

steps.d: The awarded bid, or a contract you enter directly, sets the schedule of prices.
RFIs, submittals, documents and inspections are logged against the contract as work proceeds.
Proposed changes are priced, approved and signed, and the contract value updates with them.
Progress is invoiced and certified against the same line items until the contract is complete.

faq.q: Who uses CA-Vault on a contract?
faq.a: Typically the consultant or owner’s contract administrator, the contractor, and the owner. Each sees the parts of the contract record relevant to their role.

faq.q: Does the contractor need a paid account?
faq.a: Contractor invitations are unlimited and free for contractors on paid plans. Each plan includes a set number of users for your own team, with no per-seat add-ons.

faq.q: Can I start with a contract that is already awarded?
faq.a: Yes. You do not have to tender through CA-Vault to administer a contract in it. Ask us in a demo how an in-flight contract would be brought across.

faq.q: Is there a mobile app?
faq.a: ContractComplete shipped iOS and Android apps for field access to contract documents and approvals. Current CA-Vault app availability is confirmed during your demo.

label: Document Control
title: Construction Document Control Software | CA-Vault
desc: Centralise drawings, specifications, contracts and project documents against the contract they belong to, with access for the office and the field.
short: Centralise drawings, specifications, contracts and project documents.
h1: Construction Document Control Tied to the Contract
lead: Keep drawings, specifications, contracts and supporting documents organised by contract, so the office and the field open the same file.
shotNeeded: A current CA-Vault screenshot of the contract Documents tab showing folders or document lists (2000px wide, WebP).
answer: Construction document control is the practice of keeping one current, traceable set of project documents: drawings, specifications, the contract, addenda and the records created during administration. CA-Vault stores those documents against the contract, next to the RFIs, changes and payments that reference them.
problem: Shared folders hold files, but they do not know which contract, RFI or change order a file belongs to. People end up asking which version is current, or working from the wrong one.
capsTitle: The project record, not another folder

caps.d: Documents live with the contract they govern, alongside its schedule of prices and workflows.
The documents issued at tender stay with the contract after award.
Change orders, payment certificates and invoices produced in CA-Vault are stored with the contract as PDFs.
Field staff can open specifications and drawings for the contract they are standing on.

steps.d: Attach drawings, specifications and other tender documents when you build the tender.
The document set stays with the contract as it moves into administration.
RFI responses, submittals, signed change orders and certificates accumulate in the same record.
The contract ends with a complete record rather than a folder to tidy up.

faq.q: What kinds of documents can be stored?
faq.a: Drawings, specifications, contracts and other project documents, plus the PDFs CA-Vault generates for change orders, invoices and payment certificates.

faq.q: Can contractors access the documents?
faq.a: Yes. Contractors invited to a contract can reach the documents shared on it, including from the field.

faq.q: Is there a limit on documents?
faq.a: Plans are priced by users and locations rather than by document. Ask us in a demo about storage limits.

faq.q: Does CA-Vault replace our drawing management system?
faq.a: CA-Vault is built for contract administration records, not design authoring or drawing revision management. Ask us in a demo how it would sit beside the tools you already use.

label: RFI Management
title: RFI Management Software for Construction | CA-Vault
desc: Contractors raise RFIs, consultants respond, and every question, markup and answer stays on the contract record with due dates and response tracking.
short: Keep questions, responses and supporting documentation connected.
h1: RFI Management That Keeps Every Answer on the Record
lead: Contractors raise the RFI. You respond. CA-Vault keeps the question, the markup, the answer and the dates together on the contract.
shotCaption: The RFI log with submitted, due and response dates, and response-time analytics for the contract.
answerTitle: What is an RFI in construction?
answer: A request for information (RFI) is a formal question from the contractor to the consultant or owner asking for clarification of the drawings, specifications or contract. RFI management software logs each request, routes it for a response and keeps the answer as part of the project record.
problem: RFIs sent by email are easy to miss and hard to trace. Months later, nobody can find which answer was given, when, or by whom.
capsTitle: Questions in, answers out, nothing lost

caps.d: Contractors generate a formal RFI in the platform instead of composing one from scratch.
Upload and mark up images so the question is clear before it is sent.
Each RFI is Draft, Submitted, Responded or Reopened, with submitted, due and response dates.
See total RFIs, the reopen rate and average response time for the contract.

steps.d: The contractor writes the request and attaches marked-up images.
The RFI is sent to the stakeholders who need to respond.
The consultant answers. The response is tracked and visible on the contract.
If the answer does not resolve it, the RFI is reopened rather than restarted.

faq.q: Who creates RFIs in CA-Vault?
faq.a: Contractors generate the RFI and the consultant or owner’s representative responds. Both sides see the same record.

faq.q: Can an RFI include photos or drawings?
faq.a: Yes. Contractors can upload images and mark them up so they are included in the RFI.

faq.q: How do I know an RFI is waiting for me?
faq.a: Items that need your response appear in your ActionBox, so open RFIs do not depend on someone noticing an email.

faq.q: Can an RFI lead to a change order?
faq.a: An RFI answer often triggers a change. In CA-Vault both records live on the same contract, so the trail from question to change is easy to follow.

label: Submittal Management
title: Construction Submittal Management Software | CA-Vault
desc: Receive contractor submittals, forward them to sub-consultants for review and keep every response on the contract record so reviews do not hold up the schedule.
short: Receive submittals, route them for review and keep the responses together.
h1: Submittal Management Without the Forwarding Chain
lead: Receive submittals in one place, send them to the right reviewer and keep the outcome on the contract record.
shotNeeded: A current CA-Vault screenshot of the contract Submittals tab showing a submittal log with statuses (2000px wide, WebP).
answer: A submittal is information the contractor provides for the consultant’s review before work proceeds, such as shop drawings, product data or samples. Submittal management software logs what was received, who is reviewing it and what was decided.
problem: Submittals often need more than one reviewer. Forwarding them by email makes it hard to know who has the file, and a slow review quietly becomes a schedule delay.

caps.d: Every submittal for the contract is in one list rather than across several inboxes.
Send a submittal on to sub-consultants for their review without leaving the record.
Submittals sit beside the RFIs, documents and changes they relate to.
The contractor can see where a submittal stands without phoning to ask.

steps.d: The contractor uploads the submittal against the contract.
The consultant is notified and the item is logged.
The consultant reviews it, or forwards it to a sub-consultant.
The outcome is recorded and returned to the contractor.

faq.q: Can submittals be forwarded to sub-consultants?
faq.a: Yes. Submittals can be forwarded to sub-consultants for their review while the record stays on the contract.

faq.q: Are submittals available to contractors too?
faq.a: Yes. Contractors submit through the platform and can follow the status of each item.

faq.q: How are submittals different from RFIs?
faq.a: An RFI asks a question about the contract documents. A submittal provides information for review before work proceeds. CA-Vault keeps them as separate logs on the same contract.

faq.q: Where do reviewed submittals end up?
faq.a: They remain on the contract as part of the project record through to closeout.

label: Change Order Management
title: Construction Change Order Management Software | CA-Vault
desc: Manage change orders without losing the paper trail. Track proposed changes from contractor quote through approval, signature and updated contract value.
short: Track proposed changes through approval, signature and final documentation.
h1: Manage Change Orders Without Losing the Paper Trail
lead: Take a proposed change from request and contractor quote through approval and signature, with the contract value updated as soon as it is signed.
shotCaption: Proposed changes on the left are grouped into change orders on the right, each with its value and signature status.
answer: Change order management is the process of recording a proposed change to the contract, pricing it, getting it approved and signed, and adjusting the contract value. CA-Vault handles proposed changes and change orders against the contract’s schedule of prices, so an approved change flows into progress billing.
problem: Changes are where contracts drift. When they are tracked in spreadsheets and approved by email, the signed value, the reason and the supporting evidence end up in three different places.
capsTitle: From proposed change to signed order

caps.d: Record a proposed change and request a quote. Items show as pending until the contractor prices them.
Select one or more priced proposed changes and issue them as a single change order.
See who has signed and who has not. Approve and sign from the field on a mobile device.
Download the change order as a PDF, with its supporting evidence, whenever it is needed.

steps.d: A change is proposed by the consultant or contractor, with a description of the work.
The contractor prices the change, as an addition or a credit.
Priced changes are combined into a change order and sent for signature.
Once signed, the change order is complete and its value is part of the contract.

faq.q: What is the difference between a proposed change and a change order?
faq.a: A proposed change is a change under discussion that still needs pricing or agreement. A change order is the formal, signed instruction that alters the contract. In CA-Vault, proposed changes are grouped into change orders.

faq.q: Can a change order be a credit?
faq.a: Yes. Change orders can add to or deduct from the contract value.

faq.q: Can change orders be signed electronically?
faq.a: Signatures are tracked in the platform and documents can be approved and signed on a mobile device. Ask us in a demo about your signing requirements.

faq.q: Do approved changes flow into billing?
faq.a: Yes. Because the change is recorded against the contract, the contractor can invoice against it in the same progress billing workflow.

label: Site Inspections
title: Construction Site Inspection Software | CA-Vault
desc: Capture site inspection information and supporting evidence from the field and keep it with the contract it relates to.
short: Capture inspection information and supporting evidence from the field.
h1: Site Inspections Captured in the Field, Kept on the Record
lead: Record what you saw on site, attach the evidence and keep the inspection with the contract instead of in a notebook or camera roll.
shotNeeded: A current CA-Vault screenshot of a site inspection report or the inspections list, ideally one desktop and one mobile capture (WebP).
answer: Site inspection software lets the person on site record observations, photos and deficiencies digitally and turn them into a report. In CA-Vault the inspection is stored against the contract, so it sits beside the progress, changes and payments it supports.
problem: Inspection notes written on paper have to be typed up back at the office, photos are matched to notes from memory, and the report arrives days after the visit.
capsTitle: Field evidence that supports the contract

caps.d: Record inspection information from the field rather than transcribing it later.
Keep photos and supporting evidence with the inspection they belong to.
Inspections are part of the same record as progress reports and payment certificates.
The office sees what was recorded without waiting for a write-up.

steps.d: Open the contract on site.
Capture observations and supporting evidence.
The inspection is saved to the contract record.
Use the record to support progress, deficiencies and payment decisions.

faq.q: Is the site inspections module available now?
faq.a: Site inspections is the newest module in the platform. We will confirm current availability and what it covers during your demo.

faq.q: Can inspections be completed on a phone?
faq.a: Inspections are designed to be captured in the field. Device support is confirmed during your demo.

faq.q: Where are inspection records stored?
faq.a: Against the contract, with the rest of the project record.

faq.q: Can inspections support payment certification?
faq.a: Yes. Keeping inspection evidence on the same contract gives the certifier something to refer to when reviewing progress claims.

label: Progress Reporting
title: Construction Progress Reporting Software | CA-Vault
desc: Track quantities and progress across every contract. See total value, remaining work and what can be invoiced without assembling a status spreadsheet.
short: Keep project progress and administrative records visible across every contract.
h1: Construction Progress Reporting Across Every Contract
lead: Know where each contract stands: what has been completed, what remains and what is ready to invoice, without asking someone to assemble a report.
shotCaption: The dashboard summarises projects, outstanding work, invoiceable amounts and items waiting on other people.
answer: Construction progress reporting records how much of each contract item has been completed in a period. On a unit-price contract that means quantities installed against the schedule of prices. CA-Vault uses those quantities to show progress and to feed progress billing.
problem: Progress is usually measured on site, typed into a spreadsheet, then typed again into an invoice. Portfolio status means opening every spreadsheet in turn.
capsTitle: Progress you can read at a glance

caps.d: Progress is recorded against the same items, quantities and unit prices as the contract.
Each contract shows total value, remaining value, invoiceable amount and a progress bar.
The dashboard rolls up contract value, outstanding work and approved changes across projects.
See change orders awaiting approval and RFIs awaiting response in one place.

steps.d: Enter completed quantities for the period against each item.
The progress report is saved to the contract.
Contract and company views update to show progress and remaining work.
The same quantities carry into the progress invoice.

faq.q: Can I see progress across all my contracts?
faq.a: Yes. The contracts list and dashboard show progress, remaining value and invoiceable amounts across your contracts.

faq.q: Is progress tracked by quantity or by percentage?
faq.a: Progress is recorded against contract line items, where quantity and percentage complete are shown together.

faq.q: Does progress reporting connect to invoicing?
faq.a: Yes. Completed quantities feed the progress invoice, so they are not entered twice.

faq.q: Who records progress?
faq.a: Typically the contractor records completed work and the consultant reviews it. We will show both sides in a demo.

label: Progress Billing
title: Construction Progress Billing Software | CA-Vault
desc: Contractors build progress invoices from contract line items and completed quantities, with holdback and tax applied, in one consistent format.
short: Build progress invoices from contract quantities, with holdback and tax applied.
h1: Progress Billing Built From the Contract, Not a Spreadsheet
lead: Create progress invoices from the contract’s own line items and completed quantities, with holdback and taxes calculated for you.
shotCaption: The invoice editor: holdback and tax on the left, the generated invoice with work to date and this period on the right.
answerTitle: What is progress billing in construction?
answer: Progress billing is invoicing for the portion of the contract completed in a period, rather than at the end of the job. On a unit-price contract each invoice is the quantities completed this period multiplied by their unit prices, less holdback, plus tax. CA-Vault builds that invoice from the contract record.
problem: Spreadsheet invoices vary from contractor to contractor and from month to month. One wrong formula or one stale quantity means the invoice is rejected and payment slips.

caps.d: Each invoice shows contract quantity and price, work invoiced to date and work completed this invoice.
Add holdback amounts, taxes and fees. Net value is calculated from the gross amount.
Assemble the cover sheet, line items and supporting PDFs into one invoice document.
Submitted invoices go to the consultant’s ActionBox, with reminders, so they are not missed.

steps.d: Record what was completed in the work period.
Check gross amount, holdback, tax and net value.
Submit the invoice to the consultant for review.
The consultant certifies payment against the same figures.

faq.q: Does CA-Vault calculate holdback?
faq.a: Yes. Holdback amounts can be added to an invoice and are deducted from the gross amount, and taxes and fees are added to reach the net value.

faq.q: Can change orders be invoiced?
faq.a: Approved change orders are part of the contract record and can be billed in the same workflow.

faq.q: What does the invoice look like?
faq.a: A consistent, itemised PDF showing contract values, work invoiced to date and work completed this invoice for each line.

faq.q: Does the consultant have to re-enter our invoice?
faq.a: No. When both parties work in the platform, the consultant certifies against the invoice the contractor submitted rather than re-keying it.

label: Payment Certification
title: Construction Payment Certification Software | CA-Vault
desc: Review contractor invoices and issue payment certificates from the same quantities and unit prices, without re-entering the numbers.
short: Review contractor invoices and issue payment certificates from the same figures.
h1: Payment Certification Without the Double Entry
lead: Review the contractor’s progress invoice against the contract and issue the payment certificate from the same quantities and unit prices.
shotCaption: Contract values, work invoiced to date and work completed this invoice, line by line, ready for review.
answer: A payment certificate is the document in which the consultant or contract administrator confirms the amount the owner should pay the contractor for work completed in a period. It is based on the contractor’s progress invoice, checked against the contract and the work observed on site.
problem: Certifying payment usually means re-entering the contractor’s invoice into your own spreadsheet to check it. The same numbers are typed twice, by two organisations, every month.

caps.d: Submitted invoices appear in your ActionBox, by email and in the app, with daily reminders.
See each line’s contract quantity, amount to date and amount this period on one page.
If something needs correcting, changes are made and the document is reissued rather than rebuilt.
The payment certificate is produced from the reviewed figures and kept on the contract.

steps.d: The contractor’s progress invoice arrives for review.
Check quantities and amounts against the contract and site records.
Issue the payment certificate.
The certificate stays on the contract and progress updates.

faq.q: Who issues the payment certificate?
faq.a: Usually the consultant or contract administrator acting for the owner. CA-Vault supports that review and generates the certificate.

faq.q: Do I have to re-enter the contractor’s invoice?
faq.a: No. When the contractor invoices in the platform, you review the same line items they submitted.

faq.q: What if I disagree with a quantity?
faq.a: The invoice can be revised and reissued, so the certificate reflects what was agreed.

faq.q: How do I avoid missing an invoice?
faq.a: Invoices waiting on you sit in your ActionBox and trigger reminders until they are dealt with.

label: Project Budgets
title: Construction Project Budgeting Software | CA-Vault
desc: Build a project budget on the same schedule-of-prices structure you tender and administer with, and compare bids against your budgeted price.
short: Build the budget on the same structure you tender and administer with.
h1: Project Budgets Built on the Schedule of Prices
lead: Start the project with a budget structured the same way as the tender, then compare bids against your budgeted price.
shotCaption: Switch the comparison baseline between the average bid and your budgeted price.
answerTitle: What is a construction project budget?
answer: A construction project budget is the owner’s or consultant’s estimate of what the work should cost, itemised before tender. On a unit-price project it is a schedule of prices with estimated quantities and unit rates. CA-Vault lets you carry that structure into the tender and compare bids against it.
problem: Budgets are often built in a spreadsheet that never meets the tender. When bids come in, comparing them to the estimate is another manual exercise.
capsTitle: Budget, tender and contract on one structure

caps.d: Set out items, quantities, units and estimated unit prices.
In the bid comparison, switch between the average bid and your budgeted price.
Prices above and below the baseline are highlighted line by line.
The same structure continues into the awarded contract.

steps.d: Build the budget as a schedule of prices.
Issue the same schedule to bidders.
Review bids against the budgeted price.
Move the awarded prices into the contract.

faq.q: Can I compare bids against my own estimate?
faq.a: Yes. The bid comparison can use your budgeted price as the baseline instead of the average bid.

faq.q: Is the budget visible to bidders?
faq.a: Ask us in a demo how budget visibility is controlled during a tender. We will show exactly what a bidder sees.

faq.q: Does the budget have to match the tender structure?
faq.a: Using the same structure is what makes the line-by-line comparison possible.

faq.q: Can I reuse pricing from past projects?
faq.a: Ask us in a demo about using historical pricing when building a new budget.
